newsitem.title: ITALY: Brembo sees H1 in line, eyes Far East. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brembo sees H1 in line, eyes Far East. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: Italian automotive brake maker Brembo said on Tuesday its first half performance was in line with its forecasts for 1997 which envisages sales rising 15 percent and earnings before interest and tax/sales up 10.5 percent.
The group also added at its annual general meeting that it was looking with interest at the Far East.

The group's chairman Alberto Bombassei said the company aimed to becoming more competitive and be present in growing markets, such as the Far East. He said in an interview with Reuters last year that the group was looking with interest at China, India and Brazil.
Bombassei added that in China the group had made provisional studies that could be firmed into definate plans within a year.
He added that last year's joint venture with Mexican group Sanluis was set to double sales to $80 million by 2000.

Some 40 percent of Brembo was listed on the Milan market in July 1995, and the majority is currently held by overseas investors with British investors accounting for 25 percent of the whole group and U.S. investors around eight percent.
The Bombassie family holds 56.66 percent and management just over three percent.
Brembo shares were off 4.29 percent at 19,750 lire at 1320 GMT compared to a July 1995 listing price of 11,300 lire.
